```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

This chapter follows the 2.10.4 recipe-language-2 contract. Examples are
intentionally not evaluated while the native compilers are being integrated.
Use matching client and server packages and check the server's advertised
operations before execution. A recipe describes work beside the database;
patient rows stay on the DataSHIELD server.

## Start with a study question

Suppose we want adults starting metformin, with a year of observable history,
and follow them for myocardial infarction. Concept IDs below are illustrative:
review their vocabulary definitions and descendants for your study.

```{r}
library(dsOMOPClient)
metformin <- omop_concept_set(1503297, descendants = TRUE)
diabetes <- omop_concept_set(201826, descendants = TRUE)
mi <- omop_event("condition_occurrence", 432984, descendants = TRUE)

study <- omop_study(
  index = omop_new_users(metformin, washout_days = 365,
                         select = "first_eligible", by = "ingredient"),
  require = list(age = c(18, NA),
                 has = list(omop_event("condition_occurrence", diabetes))),
  baseline = list(age = omop_age(), sex = omop_sex(),
                  visits = omop_count("visit_occurrence", before = 365)),
  outcomes = list(mi = mi),
  follow_up = list(start = 1, end = 365,
                   censor = c("observation_end", "death")),
  outputs = c("baseline", "survival"), name = "metformin_study")
print(study)
recipe_to_code(study)
```

The simple layer returns an ordinary advanced recipe. `print()` shows its
choices and `recipe_to_code()` makes them reproducible. It uses episode grain,
relative dates and priority ties. Baseline becomes a wide output; one outcome
becomes survival, while multiple outcomes become competing risk (the first
selected cause, not every later event). `long` uses outcome events; `panel`
counts them in 30-day bins. Those outputs require outcomes; baseline requires
variables. With no explicit follow-up settings, start is day 1, the end is
unbounded, and observation end and death censor follow-up.

`omop_new_users()` indexes drug eras (default gap 30 days), uses the interval
end for the episode end, and requires the washout to be observed and free of
the drug on days -365 through -1. Giving that population to `omop_study()`
keeps its index and criteria and adds `require`. The default `require$has`
looks through the index day; `no_history_of` stops the day before it.

## Make the population explicit

Use the advanced layer when the index, coverage, eligibility or output grain
needs a different policy. Here the first eligible exposure is selected; this
is deliberately an exposure-indexed example, not the era-indexed expansion of
the previous study.

```{r}
rx <- omop_event("drug_exposure", metformin)
pop <- omop_population(
  id = "users", label = "Eligible metformin starts",
  index = omop_index(rx, select = "first_eligible",
                     end = omop_end("observation_end")),
  coverage = omop_coverage(policy = "unique", on_ambiguous = "drop",
                           on_missing = "drop"),
  filters = list(
    omop_observed(before = 365),
    omop_has_not(rx, window = omop_window(-365, -1)),
    omop_has(omop_event("condition_occurrence", diabetes),
             window = omop_window(NULL, 0)),
    omop_age_is(min = 18)))

recipe <- omop_recipe(
  populations = list(users = pop),
  variables = list(age = omop_age(), sex = omop_sex()),
  outputs = list(baseline = omop_output(
    "baseline", format = "wide", rows = "users", grain = "episode",
    columns = c("age", "sex"))))
```

`first` selects a candidate before eligibility; an ineligible first candidate
can therefore leave no episode. `first_eligible` evaluates each candidate's
criteria and then selects. `all` keeps recurrent qualifying episodes. An
index offset applies before coverage lookup. By default an index must lie in
one unique observation period; ambiguous candidates are dropped privately.
`on_ambiguous = "error"` requests a bounded typed refusal instead. Union
coverage can bridge a declared gap for episode construction, but observed-day
reducers still count only recorded observed days.

Windows use inclusive whole days. A missing required anchor makes a criterion
UNKNOWN, including absence and `count == 0`; NOT of UNKNOWN remains UNKNOWN.
Only TRUE candidates survive. An available event with no rows is different
from an unavailable table: `on_missing_table = "unavailable"` makes criteria
UNKNOWN and features NA, rather than manufacturing absence or zero.

## Combine criteria and populations

A predicate inside one event must hold on the same row. Separate `omop_has()`
criteria may be satisfied by different rows. Distinct visit counts ignore
missing visit keys.

```{r}
positive_lab <- omop_event("measurement", 3004410,
                           where = omop_where(value_as_number >= 7))
criterion <- omop_all(
  omop_has(positive_lab, window = omop_window(-90, 0)),
  omop_has(omop_event("visit_occurrence", 9201),
           window = omop_window(-365, 0), distinct = "visit"))
child <- omop_population(id = "lab_users", parent_id = "users",
                         filters = list(criterion))
recipe <- recipe_add_population(recipe, child)
```

A child without its own index inherits its parent's episodes before evaluating
index-relative criteria. A child with its own index keeps those episodes and
intersects the parent's persons. Union, intersection and difference are private
population operations; small operands are allowed. Only a final published
patient component must meet `nfilter.subset`, measured in distinct persons,
not episode rows. An empty final patient component has support zero.

A persisted results cohort is another index source:

```{r}
external <- omop_population(id = "external",
  index = omop_index(list(cohort_definition_id = 42),
                     end = omop_end("event_end")))
```

Its start/end come from the cohort rows; the ordinary coverage and end rules
still apply. A cohort identifier used as a selector must be positive. Existing
`ds.omop.cohort.create()`, `.combine()` and `.from_table()` workflows remain
available; cohort handles are private inputs, not a way to retrieve rows.

## Inspect, execute and retain the inventory

```{r}
ds.omop.server.version(conns)
recipe_lint(recipe)
recipe_validate(recipe, conns = conns)
recipe_explain(recipe, conns = conns)
plan <- recipe_to_plan(recipe)
result <- recipe_execute(recipe, out = c(baseline = "D_baseline"),
                         conns = conns, on_small_site = "error")
```

`conns` is your existing DataSHIELD connection list. Explain describes the
plan and capabilities without private candidate or support counts. Execution
returns the server's committed inventory: retain it, since occupied symbol
names cause fresh names to be allocated. A partial `out` mapping publishes
only those mapped roots unless `publish` is explicitly supplied.

With the default strict server, a small final root causes federation rollback.
`on_small_site = "skip"` keeps passing sites and returns NULL for a small site.
On a non-strict server, `error` returns passing families with a warning and
`partial` status; `skip` commits nothing at that site if any family is small.
Technical failures always raise errors and trigger cleanup. The client reads
`omopPlanStatusDS` before deleting its execution symbol.

columns, including education level and cause of death.
